status: implemented and measured. All three families the QSigma-R1a gate named are now covered: tensor-network and low-treewidth by src/aionq/contraction.py, matchgate/free-fermion by src/aionq/matchgate.py. The gate is closed; the frontier is not.

amendment_matchgate.note: an earlier state of this document recorded matchgate/free-fermion as deliberately left open, on the grounds that claiming the family without implementing the strategy would be an unearned bound. That was the right call at the time and the family is now implemented rather than claimed. The finding it produced is worse than the contraction one.
amendment_matchgate.statement: T = diag(1, exp(i*pi/4)) is a Z-rotation, and Z_k = -i c_{2k-1} c_{2k} is QUADRATIC in Majorana modes, so T is a free-fermion operation. A nearest-neighbour matchgate circuit can therefore be saturated with magic and remain exactly solvable in polynomial time.

measurement.core: 12 qubits, 10 layers of T on every qubit followed by a brickwork of nearest-neighbour XXPlusYY matchgates
measurement.true_cost: polynomial time; the evolution acts on a 2n-dimensional space of Majorana operators rather than on the 2**n-dimensional Hilbert space

why_all_three_prior_strategies_miss_it.stabilizer_rank: charges alpha*T and sees only the magic, of which there is an enormous amount that costs the real simulator nothing
why_all_three_prior_strategies_miss_it.contraction: charges 2**(width+1) and sees only the connectivity; a deep nearest-neighbour circuit has width of order n whatever its gates are
why_all_three_prior_strategies_miss_it.basis_permutation: requires the core never to leave the computational basis, which a matchgate circuit does immediately

amendment_matchgate.the_severity: this is not a loose bound. An adversary can set q_sim_upper to any value on this family by padding a poly-time circuit with T gates, so on the free-fermion family the metric has no relationship to the quantity it estimates.

the_control.design: matchgates on next-nearest neighbours -- equivalently matchgates plus SWAP -- are UNIVERSAL for quantum computation, so the detector sits one gate away from certifying universal circuits as poly-time simulable
the_control.result: the same 12-qubit core with ONE SWAP appended scores 1.0000 rather than 0.0000, at identical contraction width 14
the_control.reading: the strategy distinguishes a poly-time core from a universal one differing by a single gate. Without that the addition would be worthless and dangerous.

what_the_detector_refuses_beyond_the_the: two-qubit gates must act on ADJACENT indices in the circuit's own qubit ordering, with no relabelling or routing permitted

two-qubit gates must have parity-block form G(A,B) with det A = det B, which rejects SWAP (+1 against -1), CZ (-1 against +1), CNOT (fails the block structure outright) and RZZ (whose generator Z Z is quartic in Majoranas)

one-qubit gates must be DIAGONAL. H and X involve Jordan-Wigner string operators; rather than reason about which remain Gaussian, all non-diagonal one-qubit gates are refused. A matchgate circuit written with Hadamards is missed and charged by another strategy -- a weaker bound, never a wrong one
any measurement, reset, classical bit or control flow refuses the path outright
amendment_matchgate.validation_of_the_criterion: the predicate was checked against seven gates whose free-fermion status is known independently -- iSWAP, XXPlusYY and RXX accepted; SWAP, CZ, CNOT and RZZ rejected -- before being wired into the portfolio. The two critical negatives are SWAP and CZ.
amendment_matchgate.effect_on_the_random_sweep: still 0 of 150. That generator emits no matchgates at all, so neither structural strategy fires there. Both are exercised by the K4 table and by nothing else in this repository.

subject: src/aionq/residency.py::simulation_residency, the q_sim_upper simulation-cost portfolio
statement: q_sim_upper inherited the defect it was built to retire. It prices non-Clifford content wherever it sits and never asks what that content is connected to, so a product of n independent single-qubit chains -- no two-qubit gate anywhere, a product state at every step, linear-time simulable -- scored 1.00, maximally quantum. The repository's own test suite asserted that saturation as correct.

why_it_happened.structural: section 2's 'compiler portfolio' is a minimum over four COMPILATIONS, all priced by the same stabilizer-rank cost model. It was never a minimum over STRATEGIES. Two strategies existed -- stabilizer rank at 2^(alpha*T) and basis permutation at 2^0 -- and both are blind to connectivity.
why_it_happened.the_retired_metric_made_the_same_mistake: Q_naive was retired in section 0 for scoring 1.00 on exactly classically simulable cores. q_sim_upper fixed the two failure modes that section names -- permutation embedding and Gottesman-Knill -- and reproduced the pattern on a third the section does not name: magic that is real but unconnected.
why_it_happened.why_the_suite_did_not_catch_it: tests/test_architecture.py::test_residency_scales_with_t_count witnessed the claim 'residency scales with T count' on a circuit built from h() and t() alone, containing no entangling gate at all, and asserted that it saturates at 1.00. The witness was degenerate, so the test pinned the defect as the specification. Adding a CX ladder preserves the test's intent exactly: the entangled version still saturates at 1.00.

families_at_n_12.note: no two-qubit gate anywhere; product state throughout
the crossover for this family is n=20; at n=12 stabilizer rank is still cheaper, and the table reports that rather than hiding it
CONTROL. A genuinely hard core must not be made one bit cheaper, and is not.

disconnected_block_scaling.description: k independent 2-qubit blocks on n=2k qubits, each carrying two T gates. The cost exponent is 2 for every n, so normalised residency should fall like 2/n.
disconnected_block_scaling.reading: the old column does not move, because alpha*T/n is constant when T grows in step with n. A metric that does not decay on a family whose cost exponent is fixed is not measuring structure. The new column decays like 4/n, above the truth 2/n as an upper bound must.

effect_on_the_existing_random_sweep.reading: ZERO. The ACAF generator's T-density is low enough that stabilizer rank is always the cheapest strategy, so the contraction path never wins there. This is reported rather than omitted: a new strategy that changes nothing on the existing fuzz corpus is a fact about the corpus, and stating only the constructed families would have implied a general tightening that was not measured.

the_strategy.method: build the circuit's tensor-network interaction graph -- one vertex per wire segment, a clique per gate over its 2k incident bonds -- then eliminate by minimum degree and charge 2^(induced width + 1)
the_strategy.soundness: this does not estimate treewidth and hope. It constructs a concrete elimination ordering and reports the width that ordering actually incurs, so the charge is the cost of an algorithm written down in the module. A better ordering lowers the number; a worse one cannot make it invalid.
the_strategy.convention: exponent only, matching the strategies already present: dense is charged n, stabilizer rank alpha*T, basis permutation 0, none carrying polynomial prefactors. Comparing a prefactor-carrying figure against these would be comparing two conventions.
the_strategy.fail_closed: an instruction whose unitary cannot be obtained invalidates the whole path rather than being skipped. Contraction cost is fixed by connectivity, which is available even when the matrix is not, so pricing structure alone would let a circuit be made to look cheap by adding something whose behaviour was never checked. Measurement, reset and classical control are refused outright.
the_strategy.determinism: ties in the elimination order are broken by vertex index. An ordering that depended on set iteration order would be one more computed quantity inside a reported number, which is the defect this repository has recorded five times.

amendment_saturation.note: the two amendments above ended with a diagnosis and no instrument: a portfolio missing a strategy is arbitrarily wrong on whatever that strategy was for and gives no signal about where. The signal was already present and unread.
amendment_saturation.statement: q_sim_upper == 1.0 holds exactly when log2_sim_cost >= n, which holds exactly when nothing in the portfolio simulated the core below brute force. These are UPPER bounds, so a bound at the ceiling is the absence of a bound. 1.00 never means 'measured maximally quantum'; it always means 'no applicable strategy', and it was being averaged in with real measurements.

retrodiction.method: run as a test, not asserted: disable the two structural strategies, which is the portfolio state in which both defects were live, and check which cores saturate
retrodiction.single_qubit_chains: saturated -- defect 1 would have been flagged
retrodiction.free_fermion: saturated -- defect 2 would have been flagged
retrodiction.all_to_all_magic: NOT saturated -- the genuinely hard control is not flagged, so the signal is not simply firing on everything expensive
retrodiction.random_corpus: 0 of 150 ACAF cores saturated, so the flag has no false positives there

amendment_saturation.what_the_flag_does_not_mean: saturation marks absence of information, NOT presence of easiness. A universal circuit saturates too, and correctly, because the portfolio has nothing to say about it either. The free-fermion core scored 1.00 while poly-time; one SWAP makes it universal and it scores 1.00 again. The number cannot distinguish them, and no care in reading it would have helped, because it is the same number.

monoculture_finding.measurement: recording WHICH strategy achieves the minimum shows that all 150 random ACAF cores are bounded by stabilizer_rank; the other three strategies never win on that corpus
monoculture_finding.consequence: the headline mean 0.0825 is not a portfolio result with three strategies corroborating it. It is one algorithm's output with three inactive strategies standing beside it, and a fifth strategy aimed at that regime could move all 150 at once.
monoculture_finding.relation_to_the_defects: a monoculture is precisely the condition under which both QSigma-R1a defects were possible, and the corpus never showed it because the portfolio reported only the minimum and never the argmin.

amendment_saturation.implementation: ResidencyReport gains bounding_strategy and strategy_costs, and an informative property. 'dense' is recorded as the bounding strategy when the fallback wins, because dense is not a strategy -- it is the absence of one.

amendment_no_redundancy.note: the saturation amendment showed the ACAF corpus is a stabilizer-rank monoculture. The obvious follow-up is a generator that makes the strategies compete, so that agreement between them could corroborate a bound. It was built, it works, and the result is negative.
amendment_no_redundancy.why_corroboration_is_the_only_check_avai: there is no ground truth to compare q_sim_upper against, because computing the true simulation cost is the problem the metric exists to approximate. The only evidence that a bound is not an artefact of one algorithm is that a different algorithm, pricing a different structural property, lands in the same place. Two strategies agreeing is weak evidence; one strategy unopposed is none.
amendment_no_redundancy.generator: experiments/strategy_disagreement.py, interpolating over magic density (stabilizer regime), locality (contraction regime) and matchgate fraction (free-fermion regime)

the_generator_works.reading: the monoculture is a property of the ACAF generator, not of the portfolio. Different cores really are bounded by different strategies.

the_result_is_negative.reading: nearly two thirds of cores carry a bound with nothing to compare it against, and where a runner-up exists it disagrees by a median factor of 9 in simulation cost. The corroborated region is a measure-near-zero surface, not a region.

amendment_no_redundancy.why_it_is_structural_rather_than_a_short: a minimum over upper bounds is dominated by whichever bound is best, and two differently-motivated bounds have no reason to coincide. The free-fermion path is the extreme: a single non-matchgate gate deletes it, so it cannot approach another strategy continuously. Measured, wherever it applies it wins by exactly 4 bits, and it is the only applicable strategy in 0 of 7 cases yet is never within 1 bit of the runner-up.
amendment_no_redundancy.the_sharp_form_of_remainder_1: a defect in the winning strategy is undetectable from inside the portfolio. For 63% of cores there is nothing else to check against, and where there is, it is an order of magnitude away. This is not hypothetical: it is the mechanism by which both R1a defects survived. Each was a core where one strategy was unopposed, and wrong, and nothing was positioned to notice.
amendment_no_redundancy.consequence_for_reading_the_metric: every q_sim_upper should be read as 'the best bound one named algorithm could produce', and bounding_strategy now names it. The word 'portfolio' overstates what the minimum represents.

amendment_notation_dependence.note: the no-redundancy amendment predicts that a defect in the winning strategy goes unnoticed. This is one that was, found by looking where the saturation flag fires.
amendment_notation_dependence.statement: q_sim_upper is not a function of the operator. It is a function of how the operator is written, on a metric whose stated purpose in section 0 is that it 'resists gaming by syntax and cannot be inflated by notation'.

measurement.operator: the identity on six qubits, verified by Operator(...) against the 64x64 identity at 1e-9
measurement.construction: U followed by U-dagger for a random six-qubit depth-six U, with no local cancellation visible at any optimisation level in the compiler portfolio

amendment_notation_dependence.relation_to_the_k3_suite: K3 passes all three of its equivalence attacks because the compiler portfolio cancels them. It does not reach this one. The attack is now the fourth K3 row.
amendment_notation_dependence.all_four_strategies_fail_together: every strategy either refuses the core or fails to beat dense, so the reported 1.0000 had no second opinion available. This is the no-redundancy finding in its most literal form: the correlated failure is not hypothetical.

the_flag_fires.claim: the saturation instrument was derived from two defects already known and independently marks a third that the adversarial suite passes over
the_flag_fires.significance: this is the only PREDICTIVE value the flag has demonstrated, as opposed to retrodiction of the two defects it was built from
the_flag_fires.consequence: K3 now distinguishes a wrong answer the metric flags from a wrong answer it states confidently. Only the latter counts as a kill, and this row is reported as 'GAMED but SATURATED (flagged, not silent)'.

amendment_notation_dependence.not_fixed: circuit equivalence is intractable in general and this repository has said so since the compiler portfolio was introduced. Nothing here closes the vector. What changed is that it is no longer silent.

amendment_self_review.note: a review of this round's own work, run against the same standard the round applied to the metric. Two defects were found, both of the class this round has been documenting: a guard whose witness could not reach the case it asserted.

defect_1_degenerate_saturation.what: the saturation flag reported the zero-qubit circuit as saturated -- bounding_strategy 'dense', informative False -- while q_sim_upper was 0.0
defect_1_degenerate_saturation.why_it_is_wrong: it claimed absence of information about the one circuit whose cost is exactly known, and contradicted the flag's own definition, which is the equivalence between saturation and q_sim_upper == 1.0
defect_1_degenerate_saturation.why_it_survived: test_saturation_is_exactly_the_condition_q_sim_upper_equals_one asserts that equivalence over a list of witnesses that never included n = 0
defect_1_degenerate_saturation.fix: n = 0 reports bounding_strategy 'trivial'. It has no dense ceiling to fail to beat, so saturation is not defined there rather than being defaulted to true. The witness list now includes QuantumCircuit(0) and QuantumCircuit(1).

defect_2_a_guard_that_could_not_fail.what: matchgate_plan conjugated the gate matrix by the operand swap when operands were descending, under a comment stating the parity blocks were not swap-symmetric
defect_2_a_guard_that_could_not_fail.why_it_is_wrong: they are. Conjugating by the swap exchanges basis indices 1 and 2. The eight entries required to vanish form a set closed under that exchange; A is read from {0,3}x{0,3}, fixed pointwise; B is read from {1,2}x{1,2}, conjugated and so determinant-preserving. is_matchgate_matrix is therefore invariant under the operand swap and the conjugation was a no-op on every input.
defect_2_a_guard_that_could_not_fail.why_it_survived: the test guarding it used SWAP and XXPlusYY, both symmetric under the exchange, so it passed identically whether the conjugation was present, absent or wrong
defect_2_a_guard_that_could_not_fail.measured: 0 disagreements between is_matchgate_matrix(M) and is_matchgate_matrix(swap M swap) over 4000 random and block-structured matrices
defect_2_a_guard_that_could_not_fail.fix: the conjugation is removed and the invariance it depended on is asserted directly, with an ASYMMETRIC matchgate as the witness -- identity on the even block, a rotation on the odd one -- so the property is not true by accident of the example.

checked_and_found_sound: tie-breaking in bounding_strategy awards ties in declaration order, which could make a winner histogram misleading. Measured: 0 ties in 150 ACAF cores and 0 in 216 disagreement cores, so both published histograms are strict wins and neither claim depends on the rule. The full achiever set is now recorded as bounding_achievers so a future corpus cannot hide ties.

a suspected memory blow-up from calling to_matrix() on wide gates before rejecting them: not real. to_matrix() either returns an already-stored array or raises, so MCX(11) and a 12-qubit UnitaryGate both resolve in 0.05s at under 0.1 MB.
contraction's exponent-only charge of width + 1 is the largest intermediate tensor's exponent, which no contraction in that ordering can beat, so it does not understate.
no code path serialises ResidencyReport, so the infinite entries in strategy_costs cannot reach a JSON envelope.
amendment_self_review.published_numbers_unaffected: the ACAF headline (mean 0.0825, max 0.5329, 0/150 saturated, stabilizer_rank 150), the K3 table and the K4 table are bit-identical after both fixes.

amendment_mutation_probe.note: the self-review found two guards of this round's own that could not fail, and closed with the observation that there was no instrument for that class -- the way saturation became one for missing strategies. This is the instrument, built and pointed at this round's own modules first.
amendment_mutation_probe.method: experiments/mutation_probe.py applies one meaning-changing edit to a source line -- flip a comparison, negate a condition, replace a returned constant -- and runs that module's own test file. If the tests still pass, no test distinguishes the mutated code from the real code, and whatever that line does is unguarded.

validated_against_a_known_defect_before_.why: an instrument that finds nothing proves nothing until it has been shown able to find something
validated_against_a_known_defect_before_.how: the dead operand-swap conjugation removed by the self-review was temporarily restored and the probe run against it
validated_against_a_known_defect_before_.result: line 208, 'if first > second:', SURVIVED -- the probe independently rediscovers the defect that had been found by hand

instrument_defects_found_and_fixed_befor: the comparison operators matched the arrow of a '-> str:' annotation, producing '->= str:', a SyntaxError. Those die on import for reasons unrelated to any test and inflate the kill rate with mutants no suite could survive. Measured: 4 of the first 7 contraction mutants were annotation arrows.

mutations landing inside string literals change only the text a human reads, so no test can kill them and they appear as meaningless survivors. Measured: 3 of 13 matchgate survivors were message text, a 23% noise floor in the number the instrument exists to report. Fixed by tokenising and refusing to mutate STRING and COMMENT spans.

gaps_closed: contraction: the width + 1 in the cost charge -- the whole cost convention -- could be changed to width + 0 with every test still passing, because every assertion about it was an inequality loose enough to survive an off-by-one
contraction and matchgate: summary() untested on both branches

contraction and matchgate: the refusal REASON was untested, so an 'or' could become an 'and' in the non-unitary guard with no visible effect, both clauses refusing the same instruction by different routes
matchgate: both wrongly-shaped-matrix guards could return True instead of False, since nothing ever fed either predicate an array of the wrong shape
matchgate: the 'and' in is_diagonal_matrix could become 'or', since no witness had exactly one non-zero off-diagonal entry
matchgate: the off-block entry boundary at exactly _ATOL, which IS constructible
matchgate: the is_diagonal_matrix boundary at exactly _ATOL, also constructible

the_one_remaining_survivor_is_equivalent.mutant: matchgate.py:135, '<' to '<=' on |det A - det B| < _ATOL
the_one_remaining_survivor_is_equivalent.why_it_cannot_be_killed: the two differ only when the difference equals _ATOL exactly, and np.linalg.det never returns that value. Four constructions were tried -- det A = 0 against a det B built to be 1e-9 three different ways, and det A = 1 against det B = 1 + 1e-9 -- and every one lands one ulp above at 1.0000000000000007e-09, because LU with scaling does not reproduce the literal.
the_one_remaining_survivor_is_equivalent.why_this_matters: the equivalent mutant is mutation testing's known false positive, and distinguishing it from a real gap is the difference between an instrument and a to-do list. The strictness of this comparison is not a behavioural choice; it is unobservable. A test asserts that the boundary remains unreachable, so if a future numpy makes it reachable the mutant stops being equivalent and the test says so.

amendment_mutation_probe.scope: the probe covers two modules with a fixed list of 15 operators, small enough to read in full. It is not a general mutation-testing framework and makes no claim about the rest of the repository, whose kill rate is unmeasured.

document_correction.what: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 0 printed 'q_sim_upper: mean 0.0880 max 0.7423' beside 'gap: mean 0.9175'
document_correction.why_those_cannot_both_hold: gap is defined as Q_naive - q_sim_upper and Q_naive is identically 1.0000 on this corpus, so a gap of 0.9175 IS a q_sim_upper mean of 0.0825. The page was carrying two numbers from two different runs and asserting both, while stating that every number in it is computed and none is asserted.
document_correction.attribution: re-measured on the same seed with the contraction strategy disabled and enabled, these figures are IDENTICAL. The drift predates this work and is NOT caused by the new strategy. An earlier draft of this finding attributed the change to the strategy; that attribution was wrong and is withdrawn here.

what_is_not_claimed: that the contraction bound is tight. It is the cost of one constructed ordering, and a better ordering or a better contraction scheme lowers it further.

that the free-fermion strategy covers the matchgate family. It covers a narrow, provable core of it: nearest-neighbour matchgates with diagonal one-qubit gates. Matchgate circuits written with Hadamards, or on a qubit ordering that would need routing to become adjacent, are missed and charged by another strategy. The under-claim is deliberate and can only raise the reported bound.

that closing all three named families means the portfolio is now complete. The list of families was written by the same people who wrote the portfolio, so completing it is evidence about the list rather than about the classical frontier.

that the metric is now correct. It is less wrong on one identified family. The lesson of this round is that a missing strategy is not uniformly optimistic -- it is arbitrarily wrong on whatever that strategy was for, with no signal about where.
any cognitive claim. Nothing here connects q_sim_upper to task performance; remainder point 2 is untouched.

typed_remainders.statement: The frontier this metric is 'exposed to refutation from' turned out not to be a frontier of better algorithms for hard problems. The missing strategies were the only implemented ones that could see structure at all, and their absence cost a full 1.00-to-0.17 on one family and 1.00-to-0.00 on another. A portfolio missing a strategy does not degrade gracefully.

On the free-fermion family the metric was not loosely wrong but controllable: q_sim_upper could be set to any value in [0,1] by padding a poly-time circuit with T gates that the real simulator never pays for. An upper bound an adversary can dial is not a weak bound on hardness; on that family it is not a bound on hardness. Whether any other family admits the same control is untested.

This round documented, four times, a guard whose witness could not reach the case it asserted -- and then shipped two more of its own: a saturation equivalence tested without n = 0, and a matchgate conjugation guarded by two swap-symmetric examples. Both were found by a review of this round's own work rather than by the suite, which passed throughout. The lesson is not that the reviewer was careless; it is that a test suite reports whether its witnesses fail, never whether its witnesses reach.

The mutation probe measures two modules and reports 95.7%. The rest of the repository is unmeasured, and the six defects this round found were spread across residency, the architecture tests, the part B preflight and the equivalence attacks -- none of which the probe covers. A kill rate on the two newest modules is the weakest possible evidence about the oldest ones, and it would be an error to read 95.7% as a property of the suite.

The probe had two defects of its own before its first number could be trusted: it mutated type-annotation arrows into SyntaxErrors, which inflate the kill rate, and it mutated string literals, which deflate it. Both were found by reading its output rather than by any check on the probe itself. The instrument built to detect unreached guards has no instrument detecting ITS unreached guards, and that regress is not closed here.

The identity scores 0.0000 or 1.0000 depending on the gate set it is written in, and the vector is not closed. Every q_sim_upper in this repository is a statement about a particular gate sequence, and two sequences for one operator may receive opposite verdicts. Aggregates over cores in mixed notations are therefore aggregates over an uncontrolled variable.

The portfolio cannot refute itself, and this round did not fix that -- it measured it. Adding a fifth strategy would raise the fraction of cores with a second opinion but would not change the structure: a minimum over upper bounds is still dominated by its best member. Genuine corroboration would need agreement between bounds computed by parties who did not both come from this repository, and no such comparison has been run.

The disagreement corpus is 216 cores from one cube with one seed, built by the same party that wrote the strategies being compared. It demonstrates that the ACAF monoculture is a property of that generator rather than of the portfolio, and it measures margins within its own cube. It is not a random sample of anything, and the 63.4% figure is a property of this cube, not of cognitive cores in general.

Saturation markers and measurements were being averaged together in the same mean, and the sweep's headline figure is a stabilizer-rank monoculture. Both were visible from the portfolio's own internals and neither was reported, because the portfolio published the minimum and never the argmin. The instrument for detecting a missing strategy did not need to be invented; it needed to be printed.

The free-fermion strategy sits one gate away from unsoundness. Matchgates plus SWAP are universal, and SWAP has clean parity-block structure -- it fails only on det A = +1 against det B = -1. A detector built on the block structure alone, which is the natural first implementation, would certify universal circuits as poly-time simulable and drive the metric to zero on genuinely hard cores. The safety of this addition rests entirely on one determinant comparison and on refusing all non-adjacent gates.

A test whose witness is degenerate pins the defect as the specification. test_residency_scales_with_t_count asserted saturation at 1.00 on a circuit with no entangling gate, so the suite actively defended the wrong answer. The suite's size was never the issue: 137 architecture tests passed while this one held the metric's central claim upside down.

The new strategy changes 0 of the 150 random cores. Everything demonstrated here rests on four constructed families, chosen because they exhibit the defect. That is a legitimate adversarial method and it is not a random sample: no claim is made about how often real cognitive cores fall in the low-treewidth regime.
Implemented, measured and reviewed by one party in one session. The defect it corrects was found by that same party reading its own metric, and no second party has recomputed any figure here.
